def kth_smallest_xor_walk(n, edges, s, t, k):
    """Return the k-th smallest XOR-value achievable by a walk from s to t.

    The graph is undirected. Vertices are 0..n-1 (1 <= n <= 200). `edges`
    is a list of at most 500 triples (u, v, w), each an undirected edge
    between vertices u and v (0 <= u, v < n) carrying an integer tag w
    (0 <= w < 2**30). Self-loops (u == v) and parallel edges may occur.

    A walk from s to t is a finite sequence of edge traversals that starts
    at s and ends at t. Edges may be reused any number of times, and every
    traversal of an edge XORs its tag into the walk's value once more (so
    traversing the same edge twice cancels its tag). If s == t, the empty
    walk with value 0 is a valid walk.

    Let V be the set of DISTINCT values achievable by walks from s to t
    (V is empty if and only if t is unreachable from s). Return the k-th
    smallest element of V, 1-indexed (1 <= k <= 10**18), or -1 if V has
    fewer than k elements.

    >>> kth_smallest_xor_walk(2, [(0, 1, 5)], 0, 1, 1)
    5
    >>> kth_smallest_xor_walk(3, [(0, 1, 1), (1, 2, 2), (0, 2, 4)], 0, 2, 2)
    4
    >>> kth_smallest_xor_walk(1, [], 0, 0, 2)
    -1
    """
